assumption_visibility.rationale: Six assumptions explicitly documented covering visualization adequacy, keyboard control precision, physics feasibility, test automation, docker-compose setup, and Chrome performance

evidence_grounding.rationale: Three evidence refs documented: DiscoveryCase cell_input_item with full objective specification, task metadata with process input hashes, and repository state showing no existing artifacts

problem_clarity.rationale: Problem statement clearly articulates the core value (space docking simulation), constraints (Chrome browser, keyboard controls, physical body behavior), and acceptance criteria (successful docking at airlock vs collision with hull)

risk_visibility.rationale: Four risks explicitly documented: technical challenges in realistic physics implementation and performance constraints, adoption risk from unspoken expectations about visual fidelity, and technical risk around automated test reliability with timing-dependent physics

scope_boundedness.rationale: Scope is explicitly bounded to approach and docking only, explicitly not a full game. Includes specific deliverables: physics-based simulator, rotating station with dockable airlock, collision detection, automated test, TypeScript backend, docker-compose deployment

stakeholder_coverage.rationale: Three key actors identified: requester (experience realistic docking), developer (implement TypeScript backend/docker-compose), automated test system (programmatically drive docking and validate)

unknowns_manageability.rationale: Five unknowns documented: 2D vs 3D visualization, specific physics engine requirements, frame rate expectations, automated test implementation approach, and complexity level of rotating station mechanics. These are implementation details that can be resolved during development without changing core value

non_blocking_gaps.description: Implementation detail unknowns (2D vs 3D, specific physics engine, test automation approach) can be resolved during development without changing scope or value proposition

rationale: All seven readiness dimensions are sufficient. Problem statement is clear with specific acceptance criteria. Scope is explicitly bounded to approach and docking only, not a full game. Stakeholders are well-defined. Assumptions, unknowns, and risks are thoroughly documented. Evidence is grounded in original DiscoveryCase and repository state. Recommended outcome 'go' aligns with XS complexity and well-constrained scope.
